title: Align the model by picking a face or two edges onto a G17/G18/G19 plane

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-08), part of the setup/orientation problem: "a Face or two edges should be possible to locate to a G17-G19 plane as a shortcut to the turn and tilt offset functions - this is on the model."

## What
A one-click way to orient the **model** (not the work offset) by picking geometry:

- **Pick a planar face** -> choose a target plane: **G17 (XY)**, **G18 (ZX)** or **G19 (YZ)**. The model is rotated so that face lies on/parallel to the chosen plane, its outward normal along the plane's axis (+Z for G17, +Y for G18, +X for G19; a "flip" toggle for the opposite direction).
- **Pick two edges** (two non-parallel linear edges, or two coplanar edges) -> they define a plane the same way, and the first edge also fixes the rotation about the plane normal (it is laid along the plane's first axis: X for G17/G18, Y for G19).
- Optionally, place the result: snap the picked face onto the plane's level (e.g. face to Z=0) or keep the model's current position.

It is a shortcut for the existing turn/tilt (rotate model) functions: the same rotation, computed from the pick instead of typed angles.

## Where it fits
- It acts on the **model orientation** - the part's alignment. With #326 (per-setup part alignment to the setup's frame) it should write that setup's part alignment (so a second setup can lay a different face down); until #326 lands, it uses the document-level model transform (`MoveModel`).
- It does **not** rotate the work offset (that path is #187's 3-2-1, now refused when rotated by #315/PR #325) - program zero stays a plain translation (#196 / PR #328).

## Rules
- One undoable command (the same command the rotate/tilt functions use, with the computed rotation), written on command creation.
- Refuse by name: a non-planar face; two parallel or coincident edges, or a curved edge; a degenerate face; a pick on something that is not the model.
- Stock and toolpaths react as they do to a manual rotate today (stock re-fits if it is fitted to the model; operations go stale).

## Done means
Face -> G17/G18/G19 and two edges -> G17/G18/G19 both orient the model exactly (normal within a tight angular tolerance of the target axis; edge along the target axis), undo restores the previous orientation, the refusals fire by name, pinned by app tests (rotation math on known faces/edges of a fixture block and a tilted fixture) and a UI test of the pick flow.

Related: #326 (per-setup part alignment), #316 (transform between setups), #187 (3-2-1 work offset align), #315, #196 / PR #328, #308.
